PLUGIN_HOSTD_REPLY_CODES.doc: The refusals only plugin-hostd answers by number (include/plugin-hostd/protocol.h PHD_ERRORS), and the curve verbs' own, which any host that registers them through this library answers. The numbers it answers in common with omx-clap-host are omx-clap-core's HOST_REPLY_CODES.

placementInvalid.doc: not a placement, or not valid here

noBackend.doc: no worker program for the scheme

replay.doc: the name of a refused replay on stderr, never a reply

gaveUp.doc: the storm bound is spent for that placement

verbDropped.doc: the worker died on this very command and the daemon dropped it

pinBinaryMismatch.doc: a pinned file is missing or its SHA-256 differs

lv2AdapterRefused.doc: the lv2-clap worker's LV2 adapter cannot run this plugin

noPresetList.doc: the instance's worker cannot list the plugin's presets

chainUnknownInstance.doc: a member is an instance no add made

chainDuplicate.doc: an instance is named twice in one chain

chainInstanceBusy.doc: a member is already in another chain

chainMixedFormat.doc: no one worker program runs every member

noSuchChain.doc: a chain no chain line declared

presetNotOffered.doc: a stable name the plugin does not offer

presetInvalid.doc: a preset file or path that is not the preset format

presetNeedsState.doc: a preset file that carries state for a worker that cannot take state

presetPluginChanged.doc: the preset file's plugin id, version or fingerprint is not the instance's

loadRefused.doc: the plugin refused the preset or the state its file carries

dirNotWritable.doc: descriptor_dir or qualification_dir cannot be made or written

descriptorAbsent.doc: no descriptor (panel) for the plugin's binary as it is now

descriptorPending.doc: the scan its add started has not written the descriptor (panel) yet

descriptorScanFailed.doc: the plugin's last scan wrote no descriptor (panel)

noSuchPlan.doc: a chain no plan verb planned

noRecord.doc: no qualification record names the plugin

noCell.doc: the plugin's qualification records hold no cost and latency at that rate and quantum

unknownPlugin.doc: the uri names no plugin installed here

curveKindUnknown.doc: curve_bind of a family with no closed form for the display's kind, or curve_points of a binding whose values pick a band shape or a head filter slope with no closed form

curveTermMissing.doc: curve_points of a display with no binding, or of a binding that lacks a term the model needs

curveUnitRefused.doc: curve_bind of a term in a unit its role does not take

curvePointsRange.doc: curve_points of fewer than 2 points or more than the most a curve carries, an EQ's three anchors a drawn band counted, or of a band index past what fits

durableWriteFailed.doc: the daemon's write of a file the verb changes (the history, a pin file) failed on its writer thread: the change is not on disk

writerQueueFull.doc: the daemon's writer queue holds its most writes (64) or bytes (64 MiB): the write the verb needs was refused, and nothing of it changed

curveValueNotFinite.doc: curve_points of a binding whose value, as the instance holds it, is not finite, or of an instance that runs at no rate: no curve is drawn

outputNotMonitored.doc: monitor_output_off of an output this connection did not monitor: a monitor ends with the connection that set it, and only that connection ends it earlier

PLUGIN_HOSTD_VERBS.doc: The verbs plugin-hostd adds to mod-host's protocol and answers itself, and the ones it sends a worker (README.md, Verbs the daemon adds).

workerList.doc: The workers, one record each: <core> is always -: the setting placement pins a worker to the whole set of audio cores, never to one core of its own, so no worker has a core to report; <pool> is on for a worker started with the CLAP thread pool (the pin of its plugin carries pool=cores, and no other plugin shares the worker), qualified for every other.

instanceInfo.doc: Where an instance lives and what it has cost.

supervisorReset.doc: Re-arm the storm bound and the backoff of a given-up placement: [<worker> | all].

quarantineClear.doc: Let a quarantined instance go back where its placement says: <instance> | all.

policySet.doc: The placement of an add that says default: <format | *> own | pool:<name>.

poolConfig.doc: The instances a pool holds before a sibling opens: <name> <max_instances>.

workerEnv.doc: The cpu list and the nice value of the workers of a format, at spawn and on the ones running: <format | *> <cpu-list | -> <nice | ->.

pinClear.doc: Forget the pin of one plugin, or of every one: <uri> | all.

pinReload.doc: Read the pin_file and the pins_dir files again and put the pins in at once; running instances keep running.

pinChanged.doc: The sync's notice that the pin file was rewritten: the same as pin_reload, with or without the <uri> [files|layout] of the pin_changed event.

pinAccept.doc: Under pin_mode first-use, take the plugin's files as they are now as its pin: <uri>.

pinLayout.doc: Sent by the daemon to a worker that checks layouts, after it accepted an add whose layout pin is unknown: the layout the worker found after init.

lv2WorkerSet.doc: The worker of one LV2 plugin, for its adds from now on: <uri> <mod-host | omx-clap-host | ->.

chain.doc: The instances, in this order, are one chain run in one worker: <chain> <instance> [<instance> ...]; a worker that runs chains in one client is sent the line with the members it holds.

chainClear.doc: Forget the chain: each member goes to a worker of its own.

chainGet.doc: Read a chain back: its worker, its members in the declared order, and the members its worker runs now.

descriptorGet.doc: The scanned descriptor of the plugin, answered from descriptor_dir: <uri>.

panelGet.doc: The panel the plugin publishes, answered from descriptor_dir: <uri>.

presetList.doc: The plugin's presets, the ones its preset discovery or its bundle lists.

presetGet.doc: One preset, 0 to count - 1: the key preset_load takes for it, and its name.

presetShow.doc: What a load of the preset would apply, on one line of JSON: the preset file's document with each state body's bytes replaced by its decoded size, or for a listed preset its name, loadKey and location. The instance form; mod-host's preset_show <uri> is its own verb.

historyGet.doc: What the daemon kept of one plugin on this host class, for the binary its pin holds now: <uri>. The history is one word, digest=<sha256>,class=<host class>,crashed=<0|1>,raises_xruns=<0|1> and then every key=value of PLUGIN_HOSTD_HISTORY_KEYS, joined by commas; - when the plugin has no record or no pin, unavailable while the history file is blocked.

historyClear.doc: Delete the history of one plugin, every binary and host class, or all of it: <uri> | all. Refused while the history file is blocked.

plan.doc: The instances, in signal order, are planned into the fewest workers their pins and costs allow: <chain> <instance> [<instance> ...]. Each run of consecutive members that may share a worker becomes a chain of place chain:<chain>.<k>, the others stay alone in a worker of their own; the reply names the segments in order, the members of a segment joined by commas and the segments by semicolons, then the same with each member replaced by -, the core field, which the setting placement leaves empty because it pins a worker to the whole set of audio cores and not to one core. With the setting grouping off the plan is answered and kept, and nothing moves.

planGet.doc: Read the last plan of a chain back: its segments as plan answered them, then the reason of each member that has one (a word of PLUGIN_HOSTD_GROUPING_REASONS, plan-refused followed by the refusal's number), instance:reason joined by commas, - for none, then the cores of the members as plan answers them.

planClear.doc: Forget the plan: each member goes to a worker of its own, as chain_clear does.

estimate.doc: What a chain of these plugins would cost at a rate and a quantum, read from the qualification records with no plugin loaded: <rate> <quantum> <uri> [<uri> ...], the uris as add takes them, in signal order. The reply is the latency in frames (each member's measured latency, else its declared one, added up), the CPU as percent of one core's cycle (each member's median nanoseconds per sample times the rate, added up), the RAM in bytes (the Pss each member's worker had running alone on this host class, added up; - unless every member has one), the workers plan would place the members in, and how many members have no figure at that rate and quantum; then each of those as its position in the line, from 0, and its code (noRecord, noCell or unknownPlugin), joined by commas, - for none. The latency and the CPU add up only the members that have a figure. Then the memory: what the workers hold now in bytes (- when one cannot be read), what the members would add in bytes from the qualification records, what instances of one plugin share counted once in a segment (- when no member has a figure), the host's ram_budget_mb in bytes (- when none is set), and how many members have no such figure.

PLUGIN_HOSTD_PROTOCOL_VERBS.doc: The verbs of the protocol itself, which the library answers for any host that registers them: hello (protocol_add_hello), the bulk verbs, which host_dispatch_register() answers over the host's backend, and the curve verbs, which host_dispatch_register_curve() answers over it and the rate the host gives. A client that never sends one is answered exactly as mod-host answers it.

hello.doc: Open a session: <version> [<extension> ...], the protocol version the client speaks and the extensions it asks for. The reply is the daemon's protocol version and, of the extensions asked for, the ones it grants, in the order of PLUGIN_HOSTD_PROTOCOL_EXTENSIONS; an extension the daemon does not know is not granted and is no error. Each hello replaces what the one before it granted, and a new connection starts with none. -902 for a version that is not a whole number of 1 or more, and nothing changes.

paramGetMany.doc: The values of several parameters of one instance in one line: <instance> <symbol> [<symbol> ...], each value as param_get writes it, in the order asked. A symbol the instance does not have refuses the whole line with param_get's code (-103), an instance that does not exist with -3, and no value is answered then.

paramSetMany.doc: Several parameters of one instance in one line, all or nothing: <instance> <symbol> <value> [<symbol> <value> ...]. Every pair is checked before any is set: a symbol the instance does not have (-103), an instance that does not exist (-3), a value that is not a number or a pair with no value (-902). The first pair refused refuses the line, answered resp <code> <position> with the pair's position from 1, and no value is set. Should the host refuse a value as it sets it, the values set before it are set back, and the line is refused the same way.

curveBind.doc: Bind a display of an instance's panel description to the instance's parameters, for curve_points: <instance> <display> clear, or <instance> <display> <kind> <family> <term> [<term> ...], the display's index in the description, its kind (eq_response or transfer_curve) and family, and each term <role>[.<index>]=<symbol>[:<unit>][@<shape>|<shape>...] as the description gives the role: the parameter that plays it, its unit, for a band_type the band shape of each choice value from 0 (a band_freq takes one shape, the band's fixed shape), and for a head filter's slope the dB per octave of each choice value from 0 (@12|24), the role's declared enumeration. The terms are added to the display's binding, a term of a role and index already bound replacing it; a line of another kind or family starts the binding again, and clear drops it. Every term is checked before any is kept: an instance that does not exist (-3), a symbol it does not have (-103), a family with no closed form for the kind (-536), a unit the role does not take (-538), a term the grammar does not take (-902). The binding lives with the instance and goes with its remove; it is never saved.

curvePoints.doc: The points of a bound display: <instance> <display> <points>, the grid points asked for. Each bound symbol's value is read from the instance as it is now and the instance's rate with it, and omx-dsp's omx_curve_points draws them: an eq_response x in Hz and y in dB, the bands' anchors added (three a drawn band), a transfer_curve input dB to output dB. The reply is the count and each point x,y, x to four significant digits and y to 0.01 dB, ascending in x; at most curve_points_max (omx-dsp's CURVE_POINTS_MAX, 256) points. A display with no binding, or a binding without a term the model needs (-537); a band shape or slope with no closed form (-536); points outside 2 to curve_points_max, the anchors counted (-539); a value that is not finite or an instance not running at a rate (-542).

monitorOutputOff.doc: Ends the monitor monitor_output set on an output: <instance> <symbol>, answered resp 0, and the output's feedback lines stop. A monitor ends with the connection that set it, so a controller that disconnects leaves none behind, and only the connection that set a monitor ends it earlier: an output this connection did not monitor (never monitored, monitored by an earlier connection, already ended, or its instance removed) is refused (-543), and a line that is not an instance and a symbol, or a host that does not serve the verb, is refused (-902). The output's ledger line goes with the monitor, so a respawn of the instance does not replay it.

PLUGIN_HOSTD_PROTOCOL_EXTENSIONS.doc: The extensions hello can grant, each a word a client names after its version. A session that was granted none is answered as mod-host answers it.

tags.doc: request tags: a line may start with @<tag>, and its answer then starts with the same @<tag>

errors.doc: error words: a refusal resp <n> is followed by the stable word of its code, reply.<group>.<reason>, when the protocol declares one

seq.doc: event sequence numbers: every feedback line starts with #<n>, 1 for the first after this hello and one more for each, so a gap is a missed line
